newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods' Freemans deal in UK monopoly referral.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods' Freemans deal in UK monopoly referral.

text.p: Britain's monopoly watchdog said on Tuesday it would investigate The Littlewoods Organisation's proposed purchase of mail order firm Freemans from Sears Plc.

Corporate and consumer affairs minister John Taylor said in a statement he had decided to refer the acquisition to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission in accordance with recommendations from the Office of Fair Trading.
Taylor said the planned deal raised competition concerns "in relation to the market for agency mail order catalogues in the UK." The MMC required to report by June 9.
Retailer Sears announced plans last month to sell its Freemans mail order business to Littlewoods for 395 million pounds ($645.4 million).

The deal would represent major consolidation of the British mail order market and would narrow the gap between Littlewoods and market leader Great Universal Stores Plc. The acquisition of Freemans would increase Littlewoods' market share to about 23.7 percent from 15.5 percent according to industry estimates.

Sears put Freemans up for sale as part of efforts to revitalise profits and placate digruntled investors, dissatisfied with the group's performance. Sears also promised to hand 410 million pounds to shareholders when it announced the terms of the sale to Littlewoods.
Sears' shares were two pence lower at 83.5 pence. ($1=.6120 Pound)
